key_insight: The paper reformulates LWE cryptanalysis as a penalty-free QUBO/CVP problem, letting the cryptographic noise itself become the optimization objective for a hybrid solver.
engineering_relevance: It shows how algorithm-hardware co-design can shrink encoding overhead and make LWE attacks more practical on current NISQ/Coherent Ising Machine platforms.
method: Eliminate the secret algebraically to embed LWE into a q-ary lattice and cast it as a Closest Vector Problem.
Use the squared error norm directly as the QUBO energy, avoiding penalty terms.
Apply CR-BNP-driven mixed-radix encoding to reduce qubit count and coefficient range for batched hardware execution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an end-to-end demonstration on the TU Darmstadt LWE Challenge, including a 40-dimensional Search- and Decision-LWE instance run on the Coherent Ising Machine CPQC-550.
watch_item: Performance may depend heavily on the quality of the relaxed decoding, encoding choices, and hardware noise, so scalability beyond the demonstrated instance size is not yet guaranteed.
paper_title: When the Learning With Errors Problem Meets the Coherent Ising Machine: A Penalty-Free Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design
